newsitem.title: USA: U.S. releases Korean trawler after owner pays fine.
newsitem.headline: U.S. releases Korean trawler after owner pays fine.

text.p: A South Korean fishing vessel detained in port over the weekend by U.S. officials was released on Wednesday after its owner paid a $510,000 fine for illegal fishing in the Bering Sea, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

The Cheog Yang Ho was spotted June 6 by the Coast Guard fishing illegally for pollock about 1.5 miles (2.4 km) inside U.S. territory, officials said. A Coast Guard cutter escorted the 314-foot (95 metres) factory trawler to Kodiak, Alaska, where it has been held in custody since Saturday.
The Cheog Yang Ho was released from Coast Guard custody after its owner, Korea Wonyang Fisheries Co. Ltd., electronically transferred the $510,000 to the U.S. Justice Department in Anchorage.
The payment, negotiated in a settlement, was made in lieu of possible forfeiture of the vessel, its gear and its catch, the Coast Guard said.

"Preventing illegal incursions into U.S. waters and preserving U.S. resources remains a top law enforcement priority for the 17th Coast Guard District," Capt. Norm Edwards Jr., chief of staff for the Coast Guard in Alaska, said in a news release.
"As long as there are foreign fishing vessels operating in the vicinity of U.S. waters, the Coast Guard will be on watch," Edwards said.
